note: COMPUTED FROM THE AUTHORS' TRIAL-LEVEL DATA, not read off a figure. Source: Haridi, S., Schulz, E. & Thalmann, M. (2025), 'Context Size and Set Size Effects: The Relevance of Specific Cues When Searching Long-Term Memory', Computational Brain & Behavior 9:1-33, doi:10.1007/s42113-025-00255-7; data at github.com/susanneharidi/memoryscaling, file ExperimentDataAndAnalysis/Experiment1/ExperimentDataExp1W2VSim.csv (35,856 trials; 23,896 after the preregistered participant exclusion validID, n=116). Values are the mean across participants of each participant's own accuracy (correct_01), with SD across participants. SET SIZE IS MATCHED TO THIS PORT. Experiment 1 crosses 16 set sizes from 2 to 32; this port presents 16 word pairs, so the ListLength = 16 subset is used (n=29 participants, since set sizes were assigned four per participant in blocks). Accuracy is strongly set-size dependent, so matching it matters more than the larger pooled n. Similarity bins 1-2 are taken as low and 4-5 as high, against this port's four similarity levels. Pooled across all set sizes for reference: overall 0.923 (sd 0.057, n=116), low sim 0.905 (sd 0.078), high sim 0.943 (sd 0.052). Per bin, 1 through 5: 0.913, 0.899, 0.920, 0.937, 0.950 - monotonic above bin 2, which is the similarity effect the paper reports (standardized log-odds 0.36, 95% HDI [0.18, 0.55], BF10 > 100). SUPERSEDES two earlier generations of estimate. The original 0.65 / 0.78 / 0.50 were unsourced. A subsequent pass read 0.78 off Fig. 4D and derived 0.683 / 0.854 from the reported coefficient; the data show that figure reading was WRONG by about 0.12 - actual accuracy is around 0.90, not 0.78. This is the reason to prefer archives over figures wherever an archive exists. timeout_rate 0.05 remains an author estimate: the original gave 5 s to type and asked participants to enter '0' when they could not recall, so an omission there is a response rather than a timeout.
